item.title: CrashStealer macOS Malware, ModHeader Removal, and Joomla RCE Exploitation Drive Digest
item.content:encoded:
CISA warns of actively exploited RCE flaws in Joomla extensions — Must Read

CISA warns that attackers are actively exploiting arbitrary file upload flaws in the Joomla iCagenda and Balbooa Forms extensions to achieve remote code execution and potentially take over websites. Joomla administrators should urgently update iCagenda to 4.0.8/3.9.15 and Balbooa Forms to 2.4.1 or apply mitigations.

  • CISA warned that attackers are exploiting vulnerabilities in the iCagenda and Balbooa Forms extensions for Joomla to achieve remote code execution through arbitrary file uploads.
  • CISA categorized the flaws as maximum priority and ordered federal agencies to apply available security updates or mitigations within three days, with the deadline set for today.
  • CVE-2026-48939 affects the iCagenda extension and can allow attackers to upload arbitrary files, including PHP scripts, leading to data theft, web shell installation, and complete website compromise.
  • CVE-2026-56291 affects the Balbooa Forms extension and can allow dangerous file types, such as executable files, to be uploaded, leading to remote code execution and full website takeover.
  • The flaws are fixed in iCagenda versions 4.0.8 and 3.9.15 and Balbooa Forms version 2.4.1.

CrashStealer macOS Malware Uses Notarized Dropper to Pass Gatekeeper Checks — Should Read

Researchers found CrashStealer, a new native C++ macOS infostealer delivered through a signed and Apple-notarized dropper that can pass Gatekeeper checks. It steals browser credentials, crypto wallet data, password manager data, files, and keychain material before encrypting and exfiltrating it to attacker infrastructure.

  • CrashStealer is a new macOS information stealer implemented in native C++ and analyzed by Jamf Threat Labs.
  • CrashStealer is distributed through a signed and Apple-notarized dropper named Werkbit.app, allowing it to pass Gatekeeper checks because the disk image and binary are notarized and use a valid developer ID.
  • The dropper contacts a GitHub repository to retrieve a file named sys.cache, uses it to extract a curl command, and downloads a shell script that fetches and stages CrashReporter.dmg in the /tmp directory.
  • After execution, CrashStealer establishes persistence as a LaunchAgent, validates the victim’s login password locally, unlocks the login keychain, and collects browser data, cryptocurrency wallet extensions, password manager data, keychain material, and files from Documents and Downloads.
  • The harvested data is packaged into a ZIP archive, encrypted with AES-GCM, and exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled server at 179.43.166[.]242.

Google and Microsoft Pull ModHeader With 1.6 Million Installs After Dormant Collector Found — Should Read

Google and Microsoft removed the popular ModHeader browser extension after researchers found a dormant browsing-history collection system hidden in the official Chrome and Edge versions. Although the collector’s allow-list was empty and no exfiltration was proven, it could have been activated through a routine update without new permissions.

  • Google and Microsoft removed the ModHeader browser extension from Chrome and Edge after researchers found a hidden browsing-history collector in the official store version.
  • Researchers said the collector was dormant because an internal allow-list shipped empty, and no proof has emerged that it ever collected or sent browsing domains.
  • The extension’s code could build a device fingerprint, encrypt visited domains, store up to 1,000 distinct domains locally, and post the data once a day to api.stanfordstudies.com if enabled.
  • The extension also pinged extensions-hub.com on install, update, and uninstall with the product, version, and browser.
  • Users are advised to remove ModHeader, ensure browser sync or managed policies do not reinstall it, and rotate any secrets such as API keys, bearer tokens, or session cookies that were pasted into it.

Lidl discloses online shop breach after service provider hack — Should Read

Lidl warned online shop customers in Germany, Belgium, and the Netherlands that attackers stole personal data from a file hosted by an IT service provider. Exposed data includes names, phone numbers, emails, birth dates, and customer numbers, while Lidl says it cannot yet rule out exposure of passwords, addresses, or payment details.

  • Lidl notified customers in Germany, Belgium, and the Netherlands that attackers stole personal information in a breach at a service provider.
  • Lidl said unknown individuals briefly accessed a separately stored file containing customer data, while the online shop system itself was not affected.
  • The stolen data includes online shop customers’ salutation, first and last name, telephone number, email address, date of birth, and customer number.
  • Lidl said it cannot yet rule out that affected customers’ passwords, billing and delivery addresses, bank details, or other payment information may also be involved.
  • The hacked IT service provider filed a police report and engaged IT forensic experts, and Lidl notified the Dutch Data Protection Authority.

Russian celebrity journalist Ksenia Sobchak says hackers accessed Telegram channels via email breach — May Read

Russian journalist Ksenia Sobchak said hackers briefly hijacked several of her Telegram channels through a compromised email account and posted fabricated private correspondence. The Black Mirror hacker group claims it stole more than 350GB of her data, but the authenticity of the leaked material has not been independently verified.

  • Hackers briefly took control of several Telegram channels belonging to Russian journalist and media executive Ksenia Sobchak last week and posted what they claimed were excerpts from her private correspondence.
  • Sobchak said the hackers gained access through her email account and claimed the screenshots of her interactions were fake.
  • The leaked materials carried the watermark of the hacker group Black Mirror, which claimed to have stolen more than 350 gigabytes of Sobchak's data spanning 2015 to 2026.
  • The authenticity of the leaked material and the hackers' claims could not be independently verified.
  • Sobchak runs the Ostorozhno Media holding, which operates a YouTube channel and several Telegram news channels with millions of subscribers.

Identity Due Diligence: The Missing Piece of M&A Risk Assessment — Optional

M&A cybersecurity due diligence often misses identity risk, even though exposed employee, executive, contractor, vendor, and privileged accounts can become inherited attack paths after closing. The article argues that identity exposure assessments should become a standard part of acquisitions to reduce integration risk, remediation costs, and post-deal security surprises.

  • Many M&A cybersecurity assessments focus on technical controls such as vulnerability scans, network architecture, endpoint protection, security policies, and compliance certifications while overlooking organizational identities.
  • An acquisition transfers employee accounts, executive identities, contractor credentials, vendor relationships, privileged accounts, and other digital identities into the acquiring organization’s risk profile.
  • Unidentified identity exposure can increase integration risk, disrupt operations, expand the attack surface, create regulatory and compliance challenges, and raise post-closing costs.
  • Identity Intelligence can help organizations understand exposure across employees, executives, privileged accounts, third parties, historical exposure patterns, identity concentration, and remediation priorities.
  • The article argues that identity exposure assessments, executive identity reviews, third-party identity evaluations, identity governance maturity, and exposure trend analysis are likely to become standard parts of acquisition due diligence.

⚡ Weekly Recap: ShareFile Threat, Citrix Bleed 2 Ransomware, AI Coding Attacks, and More — Optional

This week’s threats show attackers rapidly abusing trusted software, unpatched internet-facing systems, compromised packages, and AI-assisted workflows before defenders can catch up. The key takeaway is to prioritize urgent patching, close exposed services and stale sessions, and treat AI and developer tooling as critical attack surfaces.

  • Progress urged ShareFile customers to shut down Windows servers running Storage Zone Controllers due to a credible external security threat, while saying there were no indications of unauthorized access to ShareFile accounts or data.
  • Zimbra urged customers to apply updates for a critical Classic Web Client issue where a specially crafted email could run malicious code when opened and potentially expose mailbox information, session data, or account settings.
  • The Jscrambler npm package was compromised through an npm publishing credential and used to publish versions containing a Rust-based information stealer targeting developer secrets on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
  • Threat actors are exploiting Citrix Bleed 2 to deploy DragonForce ransomware, with Huntress observing a repeatable seven-step attack chain across unrelated organizations in the first half of 2026.
  • Researchers described HalluSquatting, a technique that uses AI hallucinations and prompt injections to trick AI coding assistants into installing attacker-controlled resources and running malicious code.

Breach at the Beach: Play the Ultimate Entra ID CTF — Optional

Varonis is promoting Breach at the Beach, a free Entra ID capture-the-flag training exercise focused on hands-on detection of real-world identity and data exfiltration techniques involving non-human identities and AI-era workflows. Players can earn CPE credits online or participate at Black Hat USA 2026 and DEF CON 34.

  • Varonis Threat Labs researchers Doron Kapah and Mark Vaitsman created Breach at the Beach as a free Entra ID capture-the-flag training experience focused on data exfiltration scenarios.
  • The article says Breach at the Beach is based on real customer cases involving Entra ID, non-human identities, AI agents, service principals, and automated workflows.
  • The CTF is designed to teach players how legitimate Entra ID features can be abused, how to work through raw Entra logs, and how to learn without relying on AI assistance.
  • Completing each stage of Breach at the Beach awards players 1 CPE credit and a themed badge, and completing all four stages provides a certificate of completion.
  • Varonis will feature Breach at the Beach at Black Hat USA 2026 in its booth and at DEF CON 34 in the Cloud Village, while the game is also available online.
